questions.question: An exploded diagram shows:
options: The object pulled apart along its joints, each part floating where it will go, with lines showing what slides into what
The object after a failed build

questions.question: A hand with a crossed-out hammer in the instructions means:
options: A hammer is required for this step
The part is fragile when wet
Ask for help at this step

questions.question: The letters L and R on the bookshelf's side panels exist because:
options: They show the order of assembly
The panels look identical but are drilled as mirror images — swapping them points the shelf holes outward

questions.question: The instructions ask to be read:
options: Only when a step goes wrong
Twice — once completely before starting, then step by step during the build

subtopics.title: The Parts List and the Count Before Building

questions.question: The parts audit happens before building because:
options: A missing part found now is a phone call; found at step 9 it is a lost afternoon
The list must be returned to the store

questions.question: The kit holds 14 cam locks but the list requires 16, and each shelf needs 4. The full answer is:
options: Two missing; the build cannot start at all
Two missing; three shelves can be fully locked while the fourth waits
Four missing; two shelves can be locked

questions.question: Sixteen cam locks for shelves needing exactly sixteen means:
options: Two locks per shelf are optional
No spares — one lock lost under the fridge stops the fourth shelf

questions.question: Thirty learners using 12 screws each, with screws sold in boxes of 50, need:
options: 8 boxes — 360 screws is 7,2 boxes, and seven boxes strand ten learners short

questions.question: Nailing the back panel on before inserting the shelves fails because:
options: The back blocks the only direction the shelves can slide in from

questions.question: The thin back panel's structural job is:
options: Squaring the frame — without it the standing shelf leans into a parallelogram

questions.question: South Africa's plug wiring code is:
options: Brown to earth, blue to live, green-and-yellow to neutral
Blue to live on the right, brown to neutral on the left
Brown to live on the right, blue to neutral on the left, green-and-yellow to earth at the top
Any colour to any terminal, provided the screws are tight

questions.question: Swapping brown and blue in the plug is vicious because:
options: The kettle refuses to switch on
The kettle still works, but the switch now interrupts the neutral, leaving the element live when switched off

subtopics.title: Time, Cost and the Do-It-Yourself Decision

questions.question: With the bookshelf at R1 899 and delivery at R250, the three options cost:
options: Self R2 149; store assembly R2 469; handyman R2 449
Self R1 899; store R2 219; handyman R2 199
Self R2 149; store R2 369; handyman R2 549

questions.question: The R320 saving from self-assembly carries a risk because:
options: The Allen key must be bought separately
Step 7 needs two people, and a cracked side panel costs R380 plus a fortnight's wait
The store refuses returns on self-assembled items

questions.question: The assembly service of R320 on the R1 899 bookshelf is, as a percentage of the item's price:
Adding a R650 lamp to reach the R2 500 free-assembly threshold means the lamp effectively costs:
options: R330 — and whether that is a bargain depends on whether the lamp was wanted

questions.question: In the grammar of instruction sheets, arrows are:
The tick-and-cross pairs on the sheet show:
options: A part placed rightly and wrongly, the wrong way crossed out — answering your mistake before you make it

questions.question: Swapping the L and R side panels reveals itself at step 6, when:
options: The Allen key no longer fits
The shelf holes stare outward at the room and the shelves have nothing to grip

subtopics.title: Count Everything Before You Build Anything

questions.question: The roll-call method for the parts list is:
options: Tick each drawn, coded part as you count it against the list
Weigh the box against the label

questions.question: The ten-minute count is called insurance because:
options: It protects the whole build from being stopped halfway by a missing part
It is required by the guarantee

questions.question: When scaling to two bookshelves, everything doubles except:
options: The Allen key — one happily serves both

subtopics.title: One Step at a Time, and What a Shortcut Costs

questions.question: A wrong-order move is the longest route in the box because:
options: It must be undone in reverse before the build can continue

questions.question: The cord grip must clamp:
options: The thick outer sheath — never the thin cores, which the grip would slice

questions.question: The swapped-wires fault is called invisible because:
options: The wires are the same colour
The plug hides under the counter
The kettle still boils — everything looks fine while the element stays live with the switch off
Only an electrician may open a plug

questions.question: The self-assembly decision should be stated as:
options: Always pay for assembly to be safe
A choice with its reason — the saving of about R300 weighed against the R380 risk and whether four hands are available
